A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynamicNER and CascadeNER. All 20 pages of v4 and 25 pages of v5, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original dataset-quality measurements, NER benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v5 retains the original empirical results and adds granularity-specific performance, bootstrap confidence intervals and an independent annotation-agreement study.

M1.justification: The four dynamic-categorization operations and CascadeNER’s extraction/classification cascade, entity marking, result fusion and hierarchical classification remain unchanged. Expanded strategy descriptions, prompt examples and newly disclosed LoRA settings do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v5 Section 3 and Appendix D report incorporating colloquial corpora from X and Weibo, whereas v4 describes Wikipedia-derived data. However, v5 Appendix O still states that all text comes from Wikipedia, and dataset statistics remain identical. Actual source/domain expansion and its extent are therefore unresolved. Languages and external benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmarks retain XLM-RoBERTa, GPT-NER, PromptNER, ACE+document-context, BERT-MRC+DSC and GEMNET. The removed Gemma experiments concern alternative CascadeNER backbones; the NER comparator methods themselves are unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 adds focused protocols: Base-Supervised evaluation across three granularities in English and Chinese, and a blinded two-annotator audit using 200 stratified sentences per language in four languages. Existing splits and few-shot demonstration counts remain unchanged. Appendix L supplies previously unstated training settings without establishing a revision to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds granularity-sensitivity analysis, and Appendix K adds independent human assessment of dynamic-label reliability, substantially broadening validation beyond the original categorization metrics. Conversely, v4 Appendix E.2’s Qwen/Gemma backbone ablation is removed. Result-fusion and context ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v5 Appendix G first reports 95% percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals for English and Chinese NER results using 500 test-set resamples. Appendix K adds Cohen’s kappa for annotation agreement. The existing five-trial averaging of random categorization remains unchanged; the bootstrap procedure does not establish additional independent model-training runs.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds coarse/medium results, including English C-1.5B F1 scores of 82.7/78.8 alongside the retained fine-grained 67.6. Table 13 adds kappa scores of 0.86, 0.82, 0.83 and 0.81 for English, French, Chinese and Japanese. v4 Table 9’s backbone results are removed. All matched original benchmark tables, analysis plots and cost results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same fusion, hierarchical-classification, categorization-metric and stratified-sampling mathematics. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision is added. The new statistical material describes evaluation procedures.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: an LLM-oriented dynamic NER dataset with eight languages and 155 fine-grained types, a lightweight two-stage CascadeNER framework, and comparative evaluation showing its advantages. Rewritten introductory material and additional analyses support these retained contributions without substantially redefining them.

C2.justification: v5 recommends at least two granularity levels and over 20 fine-grained types for adopting dynamic categorization, acknowledges small-dataset variance and overfitting risks, and interprets the new analyses as evidence of robustness and annotation reliability. It also attributes narrower bootstrap intervals to framework stability. The Qwen-over-Gemma interpretation disappears with its ablation; existing flat-NER and language limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix L/Table 14 adds substantial reproducibility information absent from v4: MS-SWIFT, LoRA settings, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, sequence length, checkpoint selection and GPU hardware. Appendices J/M disclose Claude-assisted annotation review and complete prompt examples. The project link changes from CascadeNER/CascadeNER to Astarojth/DynamicNER. These are documentation and access changes, without evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v5 adds references covering NERetrieve, generative NER, LoRA, parameter-efficient tuning and MS-SWIFT, and cites distinct Qwen2 and GPT-4o reports. The earlier Qwen and Gemma references are removed. These are limited citation updates and additions; the principal positioning against existing NER datasets and methods remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are extensively rewritten. New Appendix A substantially expands explanation of the existing categorization strategies, while annotation documentation is separated from the ethics statement. Author information, acknowledgements, headings and appendix organization also change, producing substantial editorial revision despite a stable methodological core.

P2.justification: Taxonomy and pipeline graphics are redrawn, prompt illustrations are revised or added, and new granularity, uncertainty, agreement and hyperparameter tables expand the presentation. Retained analysis plots are reused and relocated. The redrawn Figure 3 incorrectly labels the Czech Republic branch Person/Real Person/Athlete, replacing v4 Figure 4’s correct Location/GPE/Country labels.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses v4’s missing fine-tuning details and adds useful granularity analysis, uncertainty estimates and independent annotation-agreement evidence. These improve reproducibility and empirical assessment while the original performance results remain unchanged. Benefits are tempered by removal of the backbone ablation, contradictory corpus-source statements and incorrect labels in the redrawn pipeline. The net improvement is supported but limited.
